label: US Air Campaign Scale
description: Intensity and scope of the US air campaign against Iranian targets. As of March 29, 2026, the US has struck 11,000+ targets across 26 Iranian provinces over 29 days of sustained operations — the most intensive air campaign since OIF 2003. Strikes include B-2/B-21 stealth penetration missions, F-35 SEAD packages, carrier-based F/A-18E/F sorties from CVN-78 and CVN-77, and 1,000+ TLAMs from Virginia-class SSNs and Arleigh Burke DDGs. Trump extended the energy-strike pause to April 6, temporarily excluding oil/gas infrastructure.

source.citation: CENTCOM press releases March 2026; OSINT strike tracking via @UAControlMap and ISW; IDF operational summaries; Reuters 'US has struck over 11,000 targets in Iran' March 27, 2026

label: Iranian Air Defense Status
description: Residual operational capability of Iran's integrated air defense network after 29 days of sustained SEAD/DEAD operations. S-300PMU-2 batteries at Isfahan, Bushehr, and Tehran have been systematically targeted. Bavar-373 mobile launchers dispersed but many destroyed by F-35 sensor fusion targeting. Khordad-15 and Mersad systems largely eliminated. Some mobile short-range systems (Tor-M1, Raad) remain operational in mountainous terrain. Observed: US strike aircraft operating with near-impunity over most of Iran by mid-March.

source.citation: ISW 'Iran Conflict Update' daily briefs March 2026; IISS 'Iranian Air Defense Attrition Assessment' March 18, 2026; OSINT satellite imagery analysis via Planet Labs

label: Houthi War Entry
description: Whether Ansar Allah (Houthis) formally entered the conflict against US/Israeli forces. Confirmed: On March 28, 2026, Houthis launched ballistic missiles at Israel and claimed attacks on US naval assets in the Red Sea. This opens a second maritime front requiring US force allocation to NAVCENT Red Sea operations, complicating the Gulf-centric campaign. The Houthis demonstrated sustained missile/drone capability during the 2023-2024 Red Sea crisis despite extensive US/UK strikes.

source.citation: Ansar Allah military spokesperson statement March 28, 2026; IDF confirmation of ballistic missile intercepts; CENTCOM Red Sea threat assessment; Reuters 'Houthis enter US-Iran war' March 28, 2026

label: Hezbollah Attack Intensity
description: Level of Hezbollah military operations against Israel from southern Lebanon. Despite the November 2024 ceasefire, Hezbollah reactivated operations in solidarity with Iran following the US strikes. Observed: sustained rocket and drone attacks on northern Israel since early March 2026, though below October 2023-November 2024 peak intensity. Hezbollah's arsenal was significantly degraded during the 2024 war but retains estimated 30-40% of pre-war missile/rocket inventory.

source.citation: IDF Northern Command operational updates March 2026; UNIFIL reports; ISW 'Lebanon Conflict Assessment' March 2026; Al Jazeera 'Hezbollah resumes attacks on Israel' March 5, 2026

label: US Naval Control of the Persian Gulf
description: Degree of US 5th Fleet maritime dominance in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. The US has deployed two carrier strike groups (CVN-78 Gerald R. Ford, CVN-77 George H.W. Bush) plus an ARG/MEU. IRGC Navy's fast-attack craft and midget submarines have been systematically targeted, but mine warfare remains the primary threat to naval control. MCM (mine countermeasures) operations are underway but the US Navy's atrophied mine warfare capability — only 4 Avenger-class MCM ships remain in theater — limits clearing speed.

source.citation: CENTCOM 5th Fleet operational summaries March 2026; USNI News 'Two CSGs deployed to Gulf' March 2026; CNA 'US Mine Warfare Readiness Assessment' 2024; ONI 'Iranian Naval Capabilities' 2025

label: Iranian Asymmetric Naval Operations
description: Level of IRGC Navy and IRIN asymmetric operations in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman. Iran's naval asymmetric doctrine centers on mine warfare (2,000-3,000 mines estimated pre-war), fast-attack craft swarms (Peykaap and Zolfaghar classes), midget submarine ambushes, and shore-based anti-ship cruise missiles (Noor/Ghader). With C2 severely degraded, coordinated swarm operations are difficult, but mine-laying and individual boat attacks require minimal central coordination.

source.citation: ONI 'Iran's Naval Forces: A Tale of Two Navies' 2025; CSIS 'Iranian Mine Warfare Capabilities' 2024; CNA 'IRGC Naval Asymmetric Doctrine' 2023; CENTCOM mine threat updates March 2026

label: Cyber Warfare Intensity
description: Scale and impact of bilateral cyber operations. US Cyber Command has likely conducted offensive operations against Iranian C2, air defense radars, and missile guidance systems (precedent: Stuxnet, 2019 IRGC database wipe). Iran's APT33/34/35 groups have demonstrated capability against Gulf state infrastructure, US financial systems, and industrial control systems. Observed: multiple cyber incidents reported since conflict start, including disruptions to Iranian state media and IRGC communications, alongside suspected Iranian attacks on Gulf port systems.

source.citation: CISA advisories March 2026; Microsoft MSTIC 'Iranian Cyber Operations During Conflict' March 2026; Mandiant 'APT33/34 Activity Surge' March 2026; NSA/CSS public guidance to critical infrastructure operators

label: US Special Operations Activity
description: Level of JSOC/SOCOM activity in the Iranian theater. The US has extensive HUMINT and SIGINT networks in Iraq and the Gulf that could support cross-border operations. Historical precedent: limited SOF operations during Desert Storm, extensive in OIF/OEF. Current uncertainty: whether the administration has authorized operations beyond intelligence collection and BDA. SOF could be used for HVT targeting, pilot recovery (CSAR), sabotage of hardened facilities, or partnered operations with Kurdish/Baloch elements.

source.citation: SOCOM posture statements 2025; RAND 'Special Operations in Contested Environments' 2024; historical precedent from OIF/OEF; Seymour Hersh reporting patterns on SOF forward deployment

label: Iranian Proxy Network Coordination
description: Degree of coordination among Iran's proxy network — Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi PMF (Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq), and Syrian militia groups — in executing a unified campaign against US/Israeli forces. With IRGC Quds Force leadership decapitated and C2 severely degraded, the 'unity of fronts' doctrine is under extreme stress. Each proxy retains independent capability but synchronized multi-front operations require real-time coordination that may no longer be possible.

source.citation: ISW 'Axis of Resistance Coordination Assessment' March 2026; CSIS 'Iran's Proxy Network Under Stress' March 2026; Combating Terrorism Center 'Quds Force C2 After Decapitation' 2025

label: Conflict Duration Projection
description: Estimated total duration of active combat operations. As of March 29, the conflict is 29 days old with no ceasefire in sight. Key variables: whether the April 6 energy-strike deadline leads to further escalation; whether Iranian military capacity degrades to the point of capitulation; whether domestic US political pressure forces a halt; whether regional escalation (Houthis, Hezbollah) extends the timeline. Historical comparisons: OIF major combat 21 days, Kosovo air campaign 78 days, Libya 2011 air campaign 7 months.

source.citation: Historical air campaign duration analysis (Kosovo 78 days, Libya 213 days, OIF 21 days major combat); RAND 'Duration and Outcomes of US Military Interventions' 2024; current operational trajectory assessment

label: US Military Casualties
description: Total US military casualties (killed and wounded) during the conflict. Observed as of March 29: light casualties — approximately 30-50 wounded from Iranian ballistic missile strikes on Gulf bases (most intercepted), minor injuries from Houthi Red Sea attacks. No confirmed KIA from direct Iranian action as of reporting date. Projection forward depends heavily on whether ground operations commence and whether Iranian asymmetric attacks achieve breakthroughs.

source.citation: CENTCOM casualty reporting March 2026; DoD press briefings; historical air-campaign casualty rates (Kosovo: 0 KIA, OIF air campaign: 139 KIA first 30 days); CRS 'US Military Casualties in Operations' database

label: Iranian Military Casualties
description: Estimated total Iranian military and IRGC casualties from US strikes. With 11,000+ targets struck across 26 provinces including IRGC bases, air defense sites, missile storage facilities, naval installations, and command nodes, Iranian military losses are assessed as heavy. Exact figures are unknown — Iran has not released casualty data and independent verification is limited. Estimates from OSINT analysis of strike density and known garrison strengths suggest thousands of military KIA.

source.citation: OSINT strike analysis via ISW, Janes, and satellite imagery; historical strike-to-casualty ratios from OIF/Libya; CENTCOM BDA summaries; estimated IRGC garrison strengths per IISS Military Balance 2025

label: Nuclear Escalation Risk
description: Probability that the conflict crosses the nuclear threshold — either through Iranian breakout to a weapon (Iran had 60% enriched uranium stockpile sufficient for multiple weapons pre-conflict, with estimates of 1-2 week breakout time) or through US consideration of tactical nuclear weapons against hardened underground facilities. The Fordow enrichment facility (buried under 80m of rock near Qom) is assessed as resistant to conventional penetration. Regime desperation as military capacity collapses could drive breakout attempts, though US strikes have likely targeted enrichment infrastructure.

source.citation: IAEA safeguards reports 2025; Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists 'Iran Breakout Assessment' Feb 2026; CSIS 'Nuclear Dimensions of the Iran Conflict' March 2026; Fordow facility vulnerability analysis per NTI

label: Overall Military Balance
description: Net assessment of the military balance between US/coalition and Iranian forces. As of March 29, the balance is decisively in US favor: air superiority established, Iranian air defenses largely destroyed, command structure decapitated, missile launch capacity degraded (though not eliminated — 500+ missiles and 2000 drones launched shows residual capability). Iran cannot contest US air operations but retains asymmetric capability to impose costs through mines, proxies, and residual missile stocks.

source.citation: CENTCOM operational assessments March 2026; ISW daily conflict updates; IISS net assessment methodology; RAND 'Measuring Military Balance' applied to current operations

label: Ceasefire Window
description: Assessment of diplomatic openings for a ceasefire or conflict termination. As of March 29, negotiations are deadlocked. The US has set an April 6 deadline for the energy-strike pause — interpreted as an ultimatum to Iran. Oman and Qatar backchannel efforts are ongoing but Iran's leadership (to the extent it can communicate) has not signaled willingness to accept US terms. China has called for restraint but has not applied decisive economic pressure. The UN Security Council is paralyzed by US/Russian vetoes.

source.citation: Reuters 'Iran-US negotiations deadlocked as April deadline looms' March 29, 2026; Oman/Qatar backchannel reporting via Middle East Eye; UNSC meeting records March 2026; Trump April 6 deadline statement
